reviews.body: LGTM — reviewed the camp-as-action feature: verified the `camp-as-action` switch gates all new behavior (default on, absent false, matches features.ts), `chooseSite`/`planBuild` ignore the free `site` setting only when the switch is on (design table row 5 holds), the API refuses `set.site` with a clear message, camp sites are deterministic Reach squares with risk/misjudgement noise seeded by string keys (not the sim's RNG streams, so golden hashes are unaffected), and the acceptance tests in camp-as-action.test.ts cover all 14 listed scenarios plus app-level i18n/rendering tests. No secrets, no unrelated changes, no unsafe `any` casts.

## Focused review — determinism (openai/gpt-5)
<!-- focused lens=determinism findings=1 key=746d9aaeb70bcdf9 -->

_Result: **1 finding(s)** — any finding holds the merge (risk:high) until a new commit, which is reviewed again._

FINDINGS: 1
- src/artificer/camp-sites.ts:193 — knownSpots sorts with a comparator that can return 0 for distinct items, making the order of sites with equal priority/hours implementation-dependent.
  Fails when: two non-here, non-start spots have identical walking hours (and same atYou/start flags), the comparator returns 0 so Array.sort may preserve or reorder them differently across engines/runs, changing the default chosen spot and options order and potentially shifting downstream timing and golden hashes.

What I checked: All new/changed sim code for unseeded randomness, RNG draw order changes, nondeterministic iteration/sorting, floating-point equality use, in-place state mutation, and module-level state leaks (esp. camp-sites, region1 integration, and walking-hours cache).
